Series::gather¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::gather(std::int64_t dim, const Series& index) const -> Series

What It Does¶

Collects one element per position in index, choosing which source element along dim each output position pulls from. Every dimension except dim is walked positionally in lockstep between self and index; only along dim does index’s value pick which source row/column/… to read.

For a 2-D self and dim = 1, this is:

out[i][j] = self[i][index[i][j]]

and symmetrically for dim = 0:

out[i][j] = self[index[i][j]][j]

index_select is the special case of gather where the same index list applies to every row (or column) uniformly — gather is strictly more general, since index can vary per row.

Parameters¶

dim (std::int64_t)

Which axis index’s values are looked up along. Every other axis is matched positionally between self and index (index’s shape must match self’s shape except possibly along dim).

index (const Series&)

Integer indices into self along dim. index’s values must be in [0, self.sizes()[dim]). Indices may repeat — see the Gradient section for what that means for the backward pass.

Returns¶

Series A new Series with index’s shape, where out[..., j, ...] = self[..., index[..., j, ...], ...] (the substitution happening only along dim).

Gradient¶

gather is differentiable in self. The backward pass is a scatter_add: each output position’s incoming gradient is added back onto the exact source position gather read it from.

Warning

Repeated indices sum their gradient, they don’t overwrite it If index reads the same source position more than once, that position’s gradient is the sum of every output position that read it — not just the last one, and not split between them. See Example 2.

Examples¶

Example 1. dim = 1 on a 2×3 input: each output row picks two columns from the same-numbered input row, independently per row.

auto input = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, {2, 3});
auto index = pluss::make_series(std::vector<std::int64_t>{0, 2, 1, 0}, {2, 2});
std::cout << input.gather(1, index);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 3],
  [5, 4]]

Row 0 of index is [0, 2], so row 0 of the output is input[0][0], input[0][2] = 1, 3. Row 1 of index is [1, 0], so row 1 of the output is input[1][1], input[1][0] = 5, 4 — each row’s index list is independent, which is exactly what distinguishes gather from index_select.

Example 2. Gradient with a repeated index: position 0 is read twice, position 1 never.

auto input = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{10.0, 20.0, 30.0}, {3});
input.tracks_slope_(true);

auto index = pluss::make_series(std::vector<std::int64_t>{0, 0, 2}, {3});
auto out = input.gather(0, index);
out.sum().reverse();
std::cout << "out=" << out << "\n";
std::cout << "input.sensitivity()=" << input.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

out=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[10, 10, 30]
input.sensitivity()=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 0, 1]

index = [0, 0, 2] reads position 0 twice (into output positions 0 and 1) and position 2 once; position 1 is never read. out.sum() gives every output position gradient 1, so position 0’s two reads each contribute 1, summing to 2 — not 1, and not 0.5 each. Position 1, never read, correctly gets 0.

Notes¶

  • gather’s index must match self’s shape on every axis except dim — it does not broadcast the way maximum/minimum’s Series-argument overloads do.

  • Repeated indices are not an error; they just mean that source position’s gradient accumulates from every output position that read it (Example 2).

See Also¶

  • Series::index_select: the simpler “same index list for every row” special case of gather.
